record.original_question: Construct stationary axially symmetric 4-dimensional Ein stein metrics admitting Killing tensors of higher order. The condition "stationary axially symmetric" simply means the existen ce of two commuting vector fields, one of which is space-like and the other time-like. 11 Let us also touch upon two problems related to the homogeneous ca se. Recall that a scalar invariant of order k of a Riemannian manifold ( M, g) is a function on M, constructed from covariant derivatives of order k or less of the curvature tensor R or, equivalently, an algebraic expression in the components of covariant derivatives of R (of order ≤ k) which transforms as a function under coordinate changes. We say that ( M, g) is k-homogeneous, if all its scalar invariants up to order k are constants. It is known that, for a sufficiently big k, any k-homogeneous manifold is automatically locally homoge- neous, i.e., admits a locally transitive isometry group. As it follows from Singer [201], k = n(n+1)/2+1, where n is the dimension of the manifold, is sufficiently big in this sense; later bet ter estimations were found in [192, 54].

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A 4-dimensional pseudo-Riemannian manifold $(M,g)$ is called stationary and axially symmetric if it admits two commuting Killing vector fields, one time-like and one space-like. The metric $g$ is called Einstein if its Ricci tensor satisfies $\mathrm{Ric}(g)=\Lambda g$ for some constant $\Lambda\in\mathbb{R}$. A symmetric $(0,k)$-tensor field $K$ on $(M,g)$ is called a Killing tensor of order $k$ if $\nabla_{(i_0}K_{i_1\dots i_k)}=0$, where $\nabla$ is the Levi-Civita connection of $g$ and parentheses denote symmetrization. A Killing tensor is said to be trivial (reducible) if it is a polynomial expression with constant coefficients in the metric and in symmetrized products of Killing vector fields.

Problem: Construct an explicit example of a 4-dimensional stationary axially symmetric Einstein metric $g$ on a manifold $M$ that admits a non-trivial Killing tensor of order $k\geq 3$, or prove that no such metric exists.
artifact.status_search_result: Recent work (e.g., Vollmer 2017, arXiv:1602.08968) establishes nonexistence of nontrivial higher-valence Killing tensors for several specific stationary axisymmetric spacetimes (Tomimatsu-Sato up to valence 7, C-metric up to valence 9, Zipoy-Voorhees up to valence 11), and methodological frameworks (2024) use ansatz-based Killing tensors to recover known solutions like Kerr (which has a valence-2 Killing tensor). No explicit construction of a stationary axially symmetric 4D Einstein metric admitting a genuinely higher-order (k≥3) irreducible Killing tensor appears in the literature; the problem is widely regarded as open.

status_evidence.snippet: nonexistence of a nontrivial Killing tensor for a Tomimatsu-Sato metric (up to valence 7), for a C-metric (up to valence 9) and for a Zipoy-Voorhees metric (up to valence 11)
status_evidence.claim: Recent results rule out higher-order Killing tensors for specific stationary axisymmetric metrics, supporting that the construction problem remains open.
